label: H.R. 9393

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9393, the "Lower Costs, More Transparency Act of 2026," promotes price transparency across the U.S. health care sector. Beginning January 1, 2028, hospitals, clinical diagnostic laboratories, imaging providers and suppliers, ambulatory surgical centers, and group health plans (as well as health insurance issuers) must publicly disclose standard charges, prices, and rates in consumer-friendly and machine-readable formats. The legislation establishes compliance monitoring, enforcement procedures, civil monetary penalties for noncompliance, and specific reporting requirements for federal agencies.

affected_groups.effect: Required to compile and publish standard charges, payer-specific negotiated charges, and shoppable service prices beginning in 2028, and face potential civil monetary penalties for noncompliance.
affected_groups.group: Specified Hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals, and Rural Emergency Hospitals

affected_groups.effect: Must publicly report discounted cash prices or gross charges for specified tests, including ancillary services, beginning in 2028.
Required to make discounted cash prices or gross charges for specified imaging services publicly available on a website beginning in 2028.
Must publish standard charges and shoppable service prices in a uniform format beginning in 2028 or face civil monetary penalties.
Must maintain a real-time self-service cost-sharing tool for participants, publish quarterly rate and payment files, and submit annual compliance attestations starting in 2028.
affected_groups.group: Group Health Plans and Health Insurance Issuers

affected_groups.effect: Required to disclose applicable spread price drug information and payment-reimbursement differentials to health plans.

key_provisions: Beginning January 1, 2028, specified hospitals must publish standard charges for all items and services, prices for at least 300 shoppable services in a consumer-friendly format, provider identifiers, and an accuracy attestation using a uniform method and format established by the Secretary.

Beginning January 1, 2028, applicable clinical diagnostic laboratories must publicly post discounted cash prices (or gross charges) for specified tests along with ancillary services, update them annually, and include an attestation.

Beginning January 1, 2028, providers and suppliers furnishing specified imaging services must make discounted cash prices or gross charges publicly available on a website with annual updates and accuracy attestations.

Beginning January 1, 2028, ambulatory surgical centers must publish standard charges and prices for at least 300 shoppable services, charity care policies, and attestations in a uniform machine-readable format.

Group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual coverage must provide members with a self-service cost-sharing tool for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2028, and publicly disclose quarterly rate and payment data in machine-readable files.
Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) must disclose specified spread price drug lists and payment-to-reimbursement differences to group health plans and health insurance issuers.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for civil monetary penalties that will be specified by the Secretary for certain violations.
The specific baseline template designs and exact technical data formats the Secretary will establish prior to January 1, 2028.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9393, the "Lower Costs, More Transparency Act of 2026," promotes price transparency across the U.S. health care sector. Beginning January 1, 2028, hospitals, clinical diagnostic laboratories, imaging providers and suppliers, ambulatory surgical centers, and group health plans (as well as health insurance issuers) must publicly disclose standard charges, prices, and rates in consumer-friendly and machine-readable formats. The legislation establishes compliance monitoring, enforcement procedures, civil monetary penalties for noncompliance, and specific reporting requirements for federal agencies.
summary_detail.significance: The bill mandates widespread price transparency measures across multiple facets of the health care industry, standardizing public disclosures for hospitals, laboratories, imaging centers, ambulatory surgical centers, and health insurance plans starting in 2028. It carries extensive enforcement mechanisms, civil monetary penalties for violators, and requirements for federal agencies to submit numerous implementation reports to Congress.
